text:
Predicates:
Virus(x, y) ::: x has virus y.
Gets(x, y) ::: x gets disease y.
Animal(x) ::: x is an animal.
Mammal(x) ::: x is a mammal.
Human(x) ::: x is a human.
Symptom(x, y) ::: x has symptom y.
Fever(x) ::: x has fever.
Headache(x) ::: x has headache.
MusclePains(x) ::: x has muscle pains.
Tiredness(x) ::: x has tiredness.
Flu(x) ::: x gets the flu.
Premises:
∀x (Virus(x, monkeypoxVirus) → Gets(x, monkeypox)) ::: When the Monkeypox virus occurs in a being, it may get Monkeypox.
∃x (Animal(x) ∧ Virus(x, monkeypoxVirus)) ::: Monkeypox virus can occur in certain animals.
∀x (Human(x) → Mammal(x)) ::: Humans are mammals.
∀x (Mammal(x) → Animal(x)) ::: Mammals are animals.
Symptom(monkeypox, fever) ∧ Symptom(monkeypox, headache) ∧ Symptom(monkeypox, musclePains) ∧ Symptom(monkeypox, tiredness) ::: Symptoms of Monkeypox include fever, headache, muscle pains, and tiredness.
∀x (Flu(x) → Tiredness(x)) ::: People feel tired when they get the flu.
Conclusion:
¬∃x Flu(x) ::: No one gets the flu.
